contentEn:
Reno Stars has completed whole-house renovations across Metro Vancouver ranging from a three-month selective refresh to a twenty-two-month luxury whole-home rebuild. The honest answer to how long your project will take depends entirely on scope — and most homeowners underestimate by 30–50% when they plan based on what they have seen online.

How Long Does Each Whole-House Renovation Take in Vancouver?

Vancouver whole-house renovation timelines in 2026 break into four scopes:

  • Cosmetic refresh (selective rooms, no structural): 3–6 months
  • Mid-range full reno (kitchen, bathrooms, basement, whole home): 6–10 months
  • Premium with structural changes (load-bearing wall removal, layout reconfiguration): 10–14 months
  • Luxury or addition (designer finishes, additions, heritage restoration): 14–24 months

A cosmetic refresh keeps the existing structure intact — no demo, no rewiring, no re-plumbing. The timeline is driven by material lead times (cabinets, countertops, tile) and the speed of finishes trades in sequence. A mid-range whole-home reno involves demo to the studs, electrical re-pipe, possible asbestos abatement, and coordination of 8–12 trades — each adds a week or two of schedule. Premium and luxury scopes add structural engineering, heritage permits, and designer material lead times that individually add months.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

What Actually Extends a Whole-House Renovation Timeline in Vancouver

Five factors routinely push Vancouver whole-house timelines well past the baseline estimates above:

  • Asbestos abatement in pre-1990 homes: BC building code requires asbestos testing before demo in any home built before 1990. If asbestos is present in popcorn ceiling, pipe wrap, or floor tiles, licensed abatement adds 2–6 weeks and several thousand dollars. Some homes have it throughout — Reno Stars has seen abatement add up to $40K and 8 weeks on older Vancouver specials.
  • Knob-and-tube wiring replacement in pre-1950 homes: Knob-and-tube cannot be buried in insulation and must be fully replaced during a renovation. Replacement runs $15K–$35K and typically takes 2–3 weeks of the electrical trade alone — before other trades can proceed behind the walls.
  • Galvanized steel supply pipes: Many Vancouver homes built before 1970 have galvanized steel pipes that are rusting from the inside. A whole-house re-pipe using PEX-A runs $8K–$25K and adds 1–2 weeks to the plumbing phase. This is often discovered only when demo opens the walls.
  • Heritage and character homes: Vancouver Heritage Conservation Area restrictions require a Heritage Alteration Permit for exterior changes, design review, and in some cases specialist craftspeople for period-correct finishes. Heritage scopes routinely add 4–8 weeks to permitting alone.
  • City of Vancouver permit fees and timelines: A whole-house renovation permit package in Vancouver runs $5K–$15K in city fees alone. Structural permits, heritage permits, and occupancy permits each have independent timelines. Vancouver building department current queue is 3–6 weeks for structural permits.

Whole-House Renovation Timeline: Start to Finish

A mid-range whole-house renovation in Vancouver follows a predictable sequence:

  • Months 1–2: In-home assessment, full home survey, structural engineer assessment, permit application, 3D rendering, material selection
  • Month 2–3: Permit approval; demo begins — selective or full gut depending on scope
  • Months 3–4: Asbestos abatement if needed; electrical re-pipe; plumbing replacement; structural work (engineer sign-off)
  • Months 4–6: Rough-in inspections; insulation; drywall; mechanical rough-in
  • Months 6–8: Tile work; cabinet installation; countertop template and fabrication
  • Months 8–9: Countertop install; painting; flooring installation; fixture installation
  • Month 9–10: Final electrical and plumbing connections; appliance install; final inspection; warranty registration
  • Post-10: Punch list, final walkthrough, occupancy permit (if applicable)

How Metro Vancouver Cities Affect Renovation Timeline

Permit timelines vary across Metro Vancouver municipalities:

  • Vancouver: Structural permits 3–6 weeks; Heritage Alteration Permit (for exterior changes) adds 4–8 weeks
  • Burnaby / New Westminster: 2–4 weeks for most whole-house scopes
  • Coquitlam / Port Coquitlam: 3–5 weeks; electronic submission speeds things
  • Richmond: 2–3 weeks for most whole-house scopes
  • Surrey / Delta: 3–5 weeks depending on scope
  • North Vancouver / West Vancouver: 3–6 weeks; character home bylaws add complexity in some neighbourhoods

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the shortest whole-house renovation timeline in Vancouver?

A selective cosmetic whole-house refresh — where the scope is limited to specific rooms with no structural, electrical, or plumbing work — can run as short as 10–12 weeks. Most cosmetic refreshes, however, realistically run 3–4 months once material lead times and finishes scheduling are accounted for.

How long does a full whole-house renovation take in Vancouver?

A mid-range whole-house renovation — kitchen, two to three bathrooms, basement, flooring, electrical updates — takes 6–10 months in Vancouver. A comprehensive renovation of a 2,000–3,000 sq ft home typically runs 8–10 months. Premium scopes with structural changes extend to 10–14 months.

Does a whole-house renovation require a permit in Vancouver?

Yes. A whole-house renovation that involves structural changes, electrical re-piping, plumbing replacement, or any work that alters the building envelope requires a BC Building Code permit. In the City of Vancouver, a Heritage Alteration Permit is also required for any exterior changes to homes in a Heritage Conservation Area. Reno Stars handles all permit applications and coordinates inspections.

Can I live in my home during a whole-house renovation?

It depends on scope. For a selective renovation covering one or two floors, homeowners typically remain in the home with the work zone sealed off and a temporary kitchen set up. For a full-gut whole-house renovation involving all bathrooms and the kitchen simultaneously, most families choose to relocate for 3–6 months. We discuss living arrangements as part of our initial scope assessment.

What is the most common reason whole-house renovation timelines extend past estimate?

The most common cause is discoveries inside the walls: knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized pipes, asbestos, or structural issues that were not visible during the initial assessment. This is why Reno Stars always budgets for an engineering survey before demo — and why we include a contingency line in every fixed-price contract for exactly this scenario. Homes built before 1970 in Vancouver have a high rate of these discoveries.

溫哥華專業裝修公司聚星裝修已完成覆蓋大溫各城市的全屋裝修項目，工期從最短的 3 個月選擇性刷新，到最長的 22 個月豪華全面重建不等。影響工期的核心因素是工程範圍，而大多數業主在網上看到案例時，往往低估實際所需時間 30% 至 50% 。

溫哥華各類型全屋裝修需要多長時間？

2026 年溫哥華全屋裝修工期分為四個層級：

  • 基礎刷新（選擇性房間，無結構工程）：3–6 個月
  • 中檔全面翻新（廚房、浴室、地下室、全屋）：6–10 個月
  • 高檔結構改動（拆除承重牆、佈局重設）：10–14 個月
  • 豪華或增建（設計師用料、房屋增建、文物修復）：14–24 個月

基礎刷新保留現有結構——無需拆建、無需重鋪線路、無需改動水管。工期主要受制於建材交貨期（櫃體、檯面瓷磚）和飾面工序的進度。中檔全屋翻新涉及拆除至結構層、電線水管重鋪、可能的石棉處理，以及協調 8 至 12 個工種——每個工序都可能增加一至兩週。高檔和豪華項目涉及結構工程、文物許可，以及設計師建材交貨期，每項都可能單獨增加數月工期。

什麼因素會延長溫哥華全屋裝修工期

以下五個因素經常使溫哥華全屋裝修工期超出基本預期：

  • 1990 年前房屋的石棉處理：BC 省建築規範要求 1990 年前建造的房屋在拆建前必須進行石棉檢測。若發現石棉（吊頂、管線保溫層或地板瓷磚中存在），持證處理需額外 2–6 週及數千加元。部分老房子石棉遍布全屋——聚星裝修曾在較舊的 Vancouver 特殊房屋中見過石棉處理增加 $40,000 和 8 週工期的案例。
  • 1950 年前房屋的「knob-and-tube」線路更換：「knob-and-tube」線路不能埋在保溫層中，裝修時必須全面更換。更換費用為 $15,000 至 $35,000，僅電工工序就需額外 2–3 週——且其他工序須在此之後才能繼續進行。
  • 鍍鋅鋼供水管：1970 年前建造的許多溫哥華房屋使用鍍鋅鋼管，內壁已從內部銹蝕。全屋換用 PEX-A 管線費用為 $8,000 至 $25,000，水管工序額外增加 1–2 週。此類問題往往在拆牆後才能發現。
  • 文物及特色住宅：溫哥華文物保護區的外部改動需申請文物改造許可，並需通過設計審核，部分情況下還需聘請專業工匠處理復古飾面。文物相關項目僅許可審批就可能增加 4–8 週。
  • 溫哥華市許可證費用和審批時間：溫哥華全屋裝修許可證費用為 $5,000 至 $15,000（僅市政府收費）。結構許可、文物許可和入住許可各自有獨立審批時間。目前溫哥華建築部門結構許可排隊時間為 3–6 週。

溫哥華全屋裝修工序流程

溫哥華中檔全屋裝修遵循以下標準工序：

  • 第 1–2 個月：上門評估、全屋測量、工程師結構評估、許可證申請、3D 效果圖制作、建材選擇
  • 第 2–3 個月：許可證獲批；拆建開始——根據範圍選擇性拆除或全面拆建
  • 第 3–4 個月：石棉處理（如需要）；電線更換；水管更換；結構工程（工程師驗收）
  • 第 4–6 個月：隱蔽工程驗收；保溫層安裝；吊頂封板；機電隱蔽工程
  • 第 6–8 個月：瓷磚工程；櫃體安裝；檯面量尺及製作
  • 第 8–9 個月：檯面安裝；噴漆；地板鋪設；衛浴五金安裝
  • 第 9–10 個月：水電最終接駁；電器安裝；最終驗收；質保登記
  • 第 10 個月後：整改清單、竣工驗收、入住許可（如適用）

大溫各城市對全屋裝修工期的影响

各城市許可證審批時間有所不同：

  • 溫哥華：結構許可 3–6 週；文物改造許可（外部改動）額外增加 4–8 週
  • 本拿比 / 新西敏：大多數全屋裝修項目 2–4 週
  • 高貴林 / 滿地可：3–5 週；電子遞交可加快進度
  • 列治文：大多數全屋裝修項目 2–3 週
  • 素里 / 三角洲：根據項目規模，約 3–5 週
  • 北溫 / 西溫：3–6 週；部分小區的特色住宅附例增加審批複雜性

常見問題

溫哥華全屋裝修最短需要多長時間？

選擇性基礎全屋刷新——工程範圍限定在特定房間，無結構、電氣或水管工程——最短可達 10–12 週。然而，大多數基礎刷新在考慮建材交貨期和飾面工序排期後，現實工期為 3–4 個月。

溫哥華全面全屋翻新需要多長時間？

溫哥華中檔全屋翻新——廚房、兩至三個浴室、地下室、地板、電氣更新——需時 6–10 個月。2,000–3,000 平方尺房屋的全面翻新通常需時 8–10 個月。高檔涉及結構改動的項目，延期至 10–14 個月。

溫哥華全屋裝修需要申請許可證嗎？

需要。涉及結構改動、電線重鋪、水管更換或任何改動建築外殼的全屋裝修，均需申請 BC 省建築規範許可證。在溫哥華市，文物保護區內房屋的任何外部改動還需申請文物改造許可。聚星裝修代為辦理所有許可證申請並協調驗收事宜。

裝修期間可以繼續住在房子裡嗎？

取決於工程範圍。若工程限定在一至兩層且有可封閉的施工區域，業主通常可繼續居住，並搭建臨時迷你廚房。若為涉及所有浴室和廚房的全面拆建全屋裝修，大多數家庭會選擇暫時搬出 3–6 個月。我們在初始評估時會與業主討論居住安排方案。

全屋裝修工期延誤的最常見原因是什麼？

最常見的原因是拆牆後的「意外發現」：knob-and-tube 線路、鍍鋅鋼管、石棉或結構問題——這些在初始評估時無法看見。這就是為什麼聚星裝修在拆建前一定安排工程師勘測，並在每份固定價格合同中列入應急款項，以應對此類情況。1970 年前建於溫哥華的房屋，出現此類問題的機率很高。
